correctness.rationale: Under weak convergence and convergence of absolute first moments, the Kantorovich--Rubinstein test |x| gives the exact lower bound by the moment excess; clipping at [-R,R] gives a matching upper bound after R tends to infinity. Huang provides weak convergence of the reweighted laws and the exact perspective first-moment identity under the adopted assumptions. Uniform integrability of A_n and |B_n| gives the required primitive moment convergence. The call and put statements follow from continuous perspective integrands with a uniformly integrable linear-growth envelope, and compact-strike uniformity follows from equi-Lipschitzness. A deterministic three-atom checker independently verifies the formulas on a nontrivial signed-boundary example.

value.rationale: The result resolves a natural quantitative question left immediately by the source's exact binary boundary: how large is the first-order failure when it occurs? The answer is the same primitive boundary mass divided by the limiting numeraire mean, with a sign-resolved price interpretation. This supplies an exact metric severity and an entire compact-strike pricing signature for a boundary regime central to the source, rather than a routine recomputation or arbitrary finite slice.
